rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not ask about or consider criminal history until after a conditional offer, and may never consider non-conviction, expunged, sealed, pardoned, vacated or juvenile records. After an offer, only listed serious convictions within set look-back periods may be considered, with an individualized assessment and written reasons if the offer is withdrawn.
rules.key_value: No criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer; look-back 6 yrs (1st degree), 4 yrs (2nd/3rd), 1 yr (4th)
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer
rules.effective_date_note: Approved June 18, 2021; takes effect first day of the seventh month next following enactment, computed as 2022-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.penalty: Up to $1,000 first violation; up to $5,000 with one prior violation in 5 years; up to $10,000 with two or more prior violations in 7 years; enforced by Division on Civil Rights.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot refuse to rent to someone because of the lawful source of their income or rent payment, for example a Section 8 voucher. Complaints can be filed with the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days or in Superior Court within two years.
rules.key_value: ban on source-of-income (incl. Section 8 voucher) discrimination
rules.quoted_span: This means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income
rules.effective_date_note: Documents do not state when source-of-income protection took effect.
rules.exemptions: One apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious organization preference.
rules.penalty: Up to $10,000 for a first offense.

rules.title: NJ residential rental application fee cap ($50, CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent cannot charge more than $50 for an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental. The cap is adjusted annually for CPI, and violators face penalties, with the wrongly charged amount remitted to the applicant.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50
rules.effective_date_note: Approved 2026-01-20; effective first day of the fourth month next following enactment = 2026-05-01.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rentals other than one- or two-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Units in one- or two-family dwellings; NJ Real Estate Commission licensees unless landlord.
rules.penalty: Up to $500 first offense, $750 second, $1,000 each subsequent.

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Law – cap, handling, interest and return
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit above 1.5 times one month's rent (plus first month's rent, so 2.5 months at lease start); prepaid rent counts toward the cap, and yearly increases may not exceed 10%. Deposits are held in trust in an interest-bearing NJ account with interest to the tenant, and must be returned with interest less itemized deductions within 30 days after tenancy ends, with double damages if wrongfully withheld.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent max; return within 30 days
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (tenant may opt in by written request); seasonal rentals exempt from interest-account section.
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongly withheld plus costs and fees; tenant may apply deposit plus 7% interest to rent if notice/interest not provided.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in)

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act
rules.requirement: A landlord may remove a tenant only through court process and must have a statutory good cause (e.g., nonpayment, disorderly conduct, lease breach, conversion, owner occupancy); non-renewal also needs good cause. Except for nonpayment, a written Notice to Quit (sometimes preceded by a Notice to Cease) is required, with periods from 3 days to 3 years depending on the ground; lockouts are illegal. Owner-occupied two- and three-family buildings have a narrower set of causes under N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; Notice to Quit 3 days to 3 years depending on ground
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units (narrower rules under 61.2); transient hotel/motel or seasonal tenants; unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.
rules.penalty: Treble damages plus fees for sham owner-occupancy or removal notices; civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation.

unverifiable_exemptions: unit held in trust for developmentally disabled family member

rules.title: NJ tenant reprisal protection
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict, substantially change lease terms, or refuse to renew in retaliation for a tenant exercising protected rights, such as enforcing lease or legal rights, good-faith health or safety complaints, or joining a tenant organization. The tenant may sue for damages.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not pay for or use a coordinator's algorithmic rent-pricing software or device that uses nonpublic competitor data or facilitates parallel pricing, and no one may perform such a coordinating function. Violations are violations of the NJ Antitrust Act, and municipalities may not enact conflicting ordinances.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic coordinators / parallel pricing coordination in residential rentals
rules.quoted_span: a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;
rules.effective_date_note: Computed from section 9: first day of the twelfth month next following enactment (approved 2026-07-20); a law-firm alert (D060) also states July 1, 2027.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any rental residential dwelling unit in the State.
rules.exemptions: Research/statistical use, free public rent estimates, equal-terms brokerage databases, government affordability controls; inpatient medical, long-term care and detention facilities are not residential dwelling units.
rules.penalty: Violation of the NJ Antitrust Act; sections 6-17 enforcement applies.
rules.conflict_note: May preempt conflicting local ordinances (e.g., Jersey City § 218-12, Hoboken ch. 158, Art. II) from 2027-07-01; flag for human review.

unverifiable_exemptions: inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, detention facilities

no_rule_findings.finding: New Jersey has no statewide rent control or cap on rent increases. Municipalities may adopt rent control ordinances; increases need proper notice and must not be unconscionable. Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years after construction (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5), which limits local rules rather than creating a state cap.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.

parsed.notes: NJ final: consolidated deposit and Anti-Eviction Act candidates into one record each; reprisal kept separate. Dropped foreclosure notice and senior protected tenancy as secondary provisions from a broad handbook. The 30-year new-construction exemption is folded into the rent-increase no-rule finding, not a standalone rule. FAIR Act (eff. 2027-07-01) may preempt Jersey City and Hoboken ordinances. Link-only Justia sources not needed.
